reviews.rationale: The clause permits unlimited audits with no notice period and requires the audited party to bear audit costs only when underpayment exceeds 10%, deviating from the fallback policy that limits audits to twice per year, requires 15 days notice, and shifts cost when underpayment exceeds 5%. These gaps create a moderate exposure compared to the company's audited-rights policy.

citations.excerpt: A party may audit the other party's records relevant to this Agreement no more than twice in any twelve (12) month period, on fifteen (15) days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and subject to the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement. The audited party bears the cost only if the audit reveals an underpayment of more than five percent (5%).

reviews.suggested_fallback: A party may audit the other party's records relevant to this Agreement no more than twice in any twelve (12) month period, on fifteen (15) days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and subject to the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement. The audited party bears the cost only if the audit reveals an underpayment of more than five percent (5%).
reviews.verification_reason: The reviewer correctly cites the clause text and compares it to the playbook positions, accurately noting the unlimited audit frequency, lack of notice, and cost trigger at 10% versus the policy's limits of twice per year, 15-day notice, and cost shift at 5%. The risk rating of medium follows from this comparison, and the suggested fallback verbatim matches the playbook fallback text. All claims are supported by the provided evidence.

clause.text: 5.1 LICENSOR is the owner of all intellectual property rights, including without limitation, any and all patents, utility models, trade marks, rights in designs, trade, business or domain names, know-how, rights in databases and copyrights, rights in inventions, ideas, concepts, trade secrets and confidential information which have to be given to fulfill this contract.

The clause grants Licensor ownership of all IP needed for the contract, directly contradicting the playbook’s preferred position that each party retains its own background IP and no ownership is transferred. The playbook also states that if this provision is absent, the risk is high. Since the clause conflicts with the policy, the appropriate risk level should be high, not medium. Hence the claim is unsupported.

6.1 Each Party shall keep in confidence all material and information, including without limitation Content, received from the other Party and marked as confidential or which should be understood to be confidential, and may not use such material or information for any other purposes than those set forth in this Agreement.  6.1.1 is generally available or otherwise public; or

 6.1.2 the receiving Party has received from a third party without any obligation of confidentiality; or

 6.1.3 was in the possession of the receiving Party prior to receipt of the same from the other Party without any obligation of confidentiality related thereto; or

 6.1.4 the receiving party has independently developed without using material or information received from the other Party.

clause.text: 7.1 Unless otherwise stated in the Appendix the term of this letter Agreement shall continue for twenty-four (24) months with the effective date unless terminated sooner or extended pursuant to the terms hereof ("Initial Term").
